title: Myra Breckinridge
author: Gore Vidal
current_text: In December 1968, the Customs Department seized and confiscated a posted copy of Myra Breckinridge under Section 4A of the Customs Act. Myra Breckinridge was banned in Australia from 1968 to 1973. Gore Vidal’s biographer Fred Kaplan said that a court case in Australia concerning Myra Breckinridge resulted in a ruling that allowed Australian readers to determine what books they would read.

sources.quote: In December 1968 while on a trip to the United States I bought paperback copies of Gore Vidal’s Myra Breckinridge and Sanford Friedman’s Totempole, the former being the best-selling novel at the time in America. With a large number of other books I posted these back to myself. The Customs Department opened the parcel, seized the books and informed me they were confiscated under Section 4A of the Customs Act.

sources.quote: As the late Gore Vidal’s biographer, Fred Kaplan, noted, “In distant Australia, Myra itself became the text of a court case resulting in a ruling that allowed Australian readers to determine what books they would read” 589.
